s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain and systemic inflammation with rapid progression to multi-organ failure
salient_findings: Diffuse papules on trunk and extremities
Rapid deterioration requiring intubation and vasopressors
key_facts: Male toddler presented to emergency department
Abdominal pain and distention of 1 day's duration
Fever and vomiting of 1 day's duration
Bruises on both flanks
Diffuse papules on trunk and extremities developed over 2 days
Condition rapidly deteriorated
Required intubation, vasopressors, and empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics
Hyponatremia and neutropenia present
Elevated liver enzymes (AST and ALT)
Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Ferritin level of 603 ng/mL
Proteinuria and hematuria on urinalysis
Cavitary lesions in lungs on CT chest/abdomen
Areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys on CT chest/abdomen
Multifocal lesions on MRI brain
Punch biopsy showed small organisms within vasculature
Tissue culture, blood culture, bronchial washings, and fluid from bilateral empyemas all showed positive results

shortlist.label: Purpura fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric retiform patches and rapid progression to multi-organ failure

shortlist.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of Gram-positive cocci in vessels and positive blood culture results

shortlist.label: Meningococcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Purpura fulminans and presence of Gram-positive cocci

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid deterioration and presence of small organisms within vasculature

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome and presence of small organisms within vasculature

raw.rationale: The presence of purpuric retiform patches, rapid deterioration of condition, and laboratory findings such as hyponatremia, neutropenia, elevated liver enzymes, and high ferritin levels are consistent with Purpura fulminans, a condition characterized by thrombosis and hemorrhagic necrosis of the skin.

rejected.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
rejected.why: Although Neisseria meningitidis can cause severe sepsis, the biopsy findings of Gram-positive cocci and the lack of specific mention of meningococcal infection make it less likely

rejected.label: Meningococcemia
rejected.why: Similar to Neisseria meningitidis sepsis, the presence of Gram-positive cocci in the biopsy and the clinical presentation do not strongly support Meningococcemia

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: While the clinical presentation could be consistent with Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome, the biopsy findings and culture results showing Gram-positive cocci are more indicative of a staphylococcal or streptococcal infection, but the overall picture is more consistent with Purpura fulminans

rejected.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings could be consistent with Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome, but the presence of purpuric retiform patches and the biopsy findings are more specific for Purpura fulminans
